A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3DSRBench and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the tables, figures, equations, and image-based appendix content.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, human performance, visual-encoder comparisons, model-scaling experiments, viewpoint-robustness results, and model failure cases.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and additionally reports specialist-model comparisons in Table 2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, question transformations, CircularEval, and FlipEval procedures remain unchanged. The newly listed specialist models are comparison methods; no component of the proposed approach is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 question types using MS-COCO natural images and HSSD synthetic images with common and uncommon viewpoints. The appendix examples retain the same task and scene coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds an entire specialist comparison group: SpatialLLM, SpatialRGPT, SpatialRGPT w/depth, and SpatialReasoner. This substantially broadens comparison to methods targeting spatial reasoning. SpatialRGPT was previously cited but not evaluated in the reported tables; all existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new SpatialRGPT w/depth row introduces an explicitly depth-enabled configuration in Table 2, although depth preparation is not described. Existing splits, augmented question counts, answer extraction, and CircularEval/FlipEval procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a limited comparison between standard and depth-enabled SpatialRGPT, reporting 32.7 and 48.4 overall, respectively. No detailed controlled-ablation protocol accompanies it. The encoder/connector studies, scaling analysis, viewpoint-robustness tests, and main-text and appendix failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores without independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added specialist rows follow the existing reporting practice; CircularEval's repeated choice orderings are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds specialist results of 44.8 overall for SpatialLLM, 32.7 for SpatialRGPT, 48.4 for its depth-enabled variant, and 60.3 for SpatialReasoner. SpatialReasoner becomes the table's highest-scoring model, above the retained QWenVLMax score of 52.0. This materially expands the comparative findings; previously reported scores and qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The spatial-relation definitions and relative performance-drop formula in Section 4.3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a comprehensive human-annotated 3D benchmark, balanced evaluation with FlipEval, and evidence of limited spatial reasoning and viewpoint robustness in LMMs. The specialist results do not produce a revised core claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning implicit 3D representations, viewpoint distribution gaps, inefficient model scaling, and limitations for robotics remain substantively unchanged. V4 does not add a substantive interpretation or qualification addressing the new specialist results.

D1.justification: Appendices A and B retain the annotation pipeline and model/training descriptions. The project-link destination and CC-BY-4.0 dataset release statement remain equivalent despite the shortened abstract access sentence. No specialist-specific implementation or reproduction instructions are added.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for SpatialLLM, SpatialReasoner, and Learning to Localize Objects Improves Spatial Reasoning in Visual-LLMs, explicitly crediting the latter's left-right-bias discussion when introducing FlipEval. It removes Efficient Large Multi-Modal Models via Visual Context Compression. The broader related-work narrative remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in the abstract, FlipEval description, and model-scaling discussion. V4 also updates the author list and adds acknowledgements. The main section order and Appendices A–E remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a specialist block and rank markers with blue highlighting, changing its structure and spacing. All eleven figures and the other tables are retained, with modest typesetting and pagination changes rather than a visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: Adding purpose-built spatial-reasoning comparators addresses a relevant omission in v2's main evaluation and makes Table 2 more informative. The added attribution also better situates FlipEval. The improvement is limited because specialist-specific setup details and discussion are absent, while the established analyses, appendix evidence, and conclusions remain essentially unchanged.
